D.t: Cory Booker leads by 20.6 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 735,112 votes; a one point swing is about 17,860 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +11.5 and D +30.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Essex, a projected net 176,109 votes; Hudson, a projected net 101,769 votes; Middlesex, a projected net 82,760 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Monmouth, D +2.7, 8.0% of the vote; Morris, D +7.2, 6.4% of the vote; Gloucester, D +3.6, 3.7% of the vote; Atlantic, D +10.0, 3.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Cory Booker runs furthest behind in Gloucester, Cape May, Burlington. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 85% of voters, 61 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.27 points; White voters, 68% of voters, 52 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.42 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 56% of voters, 59 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.83 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Cory Booker: Immigration voters 25 to 72, Midsize counties 48 to 49, Voters who can afford daily costs 50 to 47. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
